newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Two killed, nine wounded in Ethiopia hotel blast.
newsitem.headline: Two killed, nine wounded in Ethiopia hotel blast.

text.p: Two people were killed and nine wounded -- including four foreign tourists -- in a grenade blast at a hotel in an ancient Ethiopian walled city, official sources said on Tuesday.
The sources said the grenade was lobbed into a hotel and exploded in the eastern city of Harar on Monday night.
The two dead were not identified but the sources said the wounded included two British women, a French woman and a German man who were tourists visiting the ancient walled eastern city.

One of the two British tourists was critically wounded and was flown on Tuesday to the Black Lion hospital in the Ethiopian capital where she was being treated in the intensive care unit, the sources said.
An official source said the other Briton was treated at the British embassy clinic in Addis Ababa and then released.
But a British diplomat said embassy staff were with the two British wounded at the Black Lion hospital and would seek the advice of doctors as to whether they should stay there or be flown to London.
There were no other details immediately available on the condition of the other seven wounded. Police in a statement in Addis Ababa said they were searching for the attackers.

Ethiopian authorities last year blamed Moslem fundamentalist "terrorists" for a series of bomb attacks in the east and the capital and sent troops in August on a two-day incursion into western Somalia to destroy several bases and training camps.
Unidentified gunmen shot and wounded Ethiopian Transport and Communications Minister Abdulmejid Hussein, who is of Somali ethnic origin and from the east, in July last year in Addis Ababa.
The Ethiopian government vowed to send its forces back into Somalia, which has had no central government since the overthrow of dictator, should it be necessary to stop the attacks in its territory.
The Somali Moslem fundamentalist al-Ittihad al-Islami (Islamic Union) movement said Ethiopian troops backed by tanks invaded western Somalia again in September and December to hit its bases.
It declared a "jihad" (holy war) against Addis Ababa and said its forces would hit back both in Ethiopia and Somalia.
A total of 15 people were killed in May 1995 when attackers tossed a hand grenade into a bustling market in the town of Dire Dawa, which is also in the eastern region of Harraghe.
Six other people were killed in 1995 in a bomb blast at the Ghion Hotel, one of the largest government-owned hotels in Addis Ababa.
A bomb killed one person and wounded a total of 11 others at the Wabe Shebelle hotel in Addis Ababa in August last year.
